Naomi / team,

Quick guidance after reviewing the bank letter and resolution:

- The bank letter and corporate resolution are good supporting documents for identity and signing authority. The bank letter must be recent (ours say within 90 days) and on bank letterhead; the copy provided looks acceptable for intake.
- For a chapter 3 treaty claim on a W-8BEN-E, the IRS prefers that the beneficial owner provide a U.S. TIN when claiming reduced withholding. In practice we have accepted treaty claims without a U.S. TIN in narrow cases if the vendor provides strong supporting docs and signs a declaration committing to obtain a U.S. TIN within a defined period.
- Recommended path: offer Sinocean a conditional PO (PO-78945) with the following terms: 1) Redwood will issue a limited-scope PO to begin integration work; 2) Sinocean must obtain and deliver a U.S. EIN (or provide an IRS-issued substitute like Form 6166 if applicable) within 60 calendar days; 3) If EIN isn’t provided within 60 days, Redwood will apply statutory 30% withholding to amounts subject to chapter 3 or reserve payment until cleared.
- Document retention: store copies of W-8BEN-E, bank letter, corporate resolution, and vendor’s written commitment to apply for EIN in the vendor file. That will support our withholding position if audited.

If Sinocean prefers to wait for an EIN before we issue the PO, procurement can hold — but that will delay their start. If procurement wants to proceed, set the PO as conditional and add the withholding fallback.

I’ll draft a short conditional PO clause you can use.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Tax Counsel, Redwood Inference
